text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1% today, extending a two-week decline that has now cost the stock about 1.8%. The most concrete headwind is the geopolitical backdrop: while Middle East tensions have kept crude prices elevated (U.S. oil at $96/barrel, global at nearly $115), renewed diplomatic talks between the U.S. and Iran are signaling potential de-escalation, which typically weighs on energy prices and refiner margins. At the same time, refineries are running near full capacity (94%), but gasoline and diesel inventories remain relatively high, limiting the pricing power refiners can extract from processing crude into finished products.

The broader risk is the policy uncertainty around diesel exports—potential restrictions could disrupt refiner economics by forcing adjustments to production mix and potentially squeezing margins as global supply tightens. Combined with the structural squeeze between high crude costs and moderate product prices, refiners like Marathon face a challenging near-term environment even as utilization remains strong.
